title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Title: 'Local "Lefschetz" conjectures'. Setup: S = Spec A with A a strictly local (strictly henselian) excellent ring, and f in m_A. My reading of 'X = S - pt fermé' (the transcription has 'S-lt fini') is that X is the punctured spectrum. Then Y = X ∩ V(f) is the punctured spectrum of A/f. 'X, Y réguliers' then means A and A/f have isolated singularities, and U = X - Y. N = dim A, so X is the punctured spectrum of an N-dimensional isolated singularity.

Notation, following the Chow-group notation in this dossier:
- A^i = codimension-i Chow group.
- J^i = subgroup of cycles algebraically equivalent to zero (the 'Jacobian' or continuous part).
- N^i = A^i/J^i, the Néron–Severi-type discrete part.
So A^i is an extension of N^i by J^i.

Conjecture (1), a vanishing range for one punctured spectrum:
- N^i(X) is finite (≡ 0 modulo finite groups) for i ≥ N/2.
- J^i(X) = 0 and N^i(X) ≡ 0 for i ≥ (N+1)/2.
- Hence A^i(X) is finite in that range.

Conjecture (2), a local Lefschetz theorem for restriction to the hypersurface section Y.
- J^i(X) → J^i(Y) is bijective (except p-torsion) for i ≤ (N-2)/2 and injective for i ≤ (N-1)/2. It is zero for i ≥ N/2, trivially, since (1) applied to Y (dimension N-1) gives J^i(Y) = 0.
- N^i(X) → N^i(Y) is bijective for i ≤ (N-3)/2, injective for i ≤ (N-2)/2, and zero mod finite for i ≥ (N-1)/2.
- The bracketed N.B.s check these against (1) for X and Y.
- The critical cases are J^{(N-1)/2}, J^{N/2}, and on the next page N^{(N-2)/2}, N^{(N-1)/2}.

The next page adds:
- (3) statements comparing A^i(X) with A^i(U) via localization.
- (4) a problem: define intersection forms N^i(X) × N^i(X) → Z and a 'theory of vanishing cycles' governing the critical maps.
- The check N = 2: N^1(X) = Cl(A) mod algebraic equivalence is finite. This is Mumford's theorem (negative-definite intersection matrix of a resolution), and the essential group is J^1(X) (Pic^0 of the exceptional fibre).

Purpose: extend the SGA2 local Lefschetz theorems for local Picard groups to all Chow groups of punctured spectra. Those theorems are Grothendieck–Samuel: complete intersections of dimension ≥ 4 are factorial. The extension is modelled on the topology of the link of an isolated singularity, a (2N-1)-manifold.
errors: If X were taken to be a regular local scheme itself, A^i(X) = 0 for i ≥ 1 (codim 1: factoriality; higher codim via Gersten), making everything trivial. The intended object must be the punctured spectrum of an isolated singularity, so the transcription 'S-lt fini' is likely a misreading.
Internal consistency is good: the 'nul' ranges in (2) follow from applying (1) to Y of dimension N-1, as the N.B.s note.

The '?' on 'N^i(X) = N^i(Y) = 0 if i ≥ N/2' is justified: (1) only yields vanishing modulo finite groups. Strict vanishing would be false in general because of torsion, e.g. Cl of an A_n surface singularity is Z/(n+1).

For general (non-complete-intersection) isolated singularities the Lefschetz ranges in (2) cannot hold without extra depth or cohomological hypotheses; even for Pic, SGA2 needs depth conditions. Presumably complete-intersection-type hypotheses are implicit.

The attribution 'Mumford(-Hodge)' for N=2 is apt in spirit (negative definiteness, Hodge-index type). The precise structure theorem, Cl = finite group extended by Pic^0, is usually credited to Mumford 1961 together with Lipman 1969.

ideas.what: Lefschetz-type comparison of Chow groups (discrete part N^i and continuous part J^i) of the punctured spectrum X of an isolated singularity with those of a hypersurface section Y, with explicit ranges i ≤ (N-3)/2, (N-2)/2, (N-1)/2
ideas.modern_name: Grothendieck–Lefschetz theorems for Chow groups of local rings / punctured spectra
ideas.usually_credited_to: Codimension 1: Grothendieck (SGA2, 1962) and Samuel's conjecture; later Robbiano, Ravindra–Srinivas, Kollár (local class groups). Higher codimension: largely open, with partial work by Srinivas, Kurano, Roberts.
ideas.where_published: SGA2 Exp. XI–XIII contains the Pic and π1/cohomology versions and conjectures; I do not know of a published higher-codimension Chow version

ideas.what: Vanishing modulo finite groups of N^i(X) for i ≥ N/2 and of J^i(X) for i ≥ (N+1)/2 on the punctured spectrum
ideas.modern_name: Finiteness of high-codimension Chow groups of isolated singularities; reflects weight (semi-purity) properties of link cohomology
ideas.usually_credited_to: Hodge side: Steenbrink, Durfee, Gabber purity (weights of H^k of the link are ≤ k for k < N and > k for k ≥ N). Chow side: Srinivas, Kurano (conjectural).

ideas.what: Request for intersection forms on N^i of the punctured spectrum and a 'vanishing cycle' theory controlling the critical Lefschetz degrees
ideas.modern_name: Numerical equivalence on Chow groups of local rings (Kurano–Roberts); Hochster theta pairing / linking forms (Buchweitz–van Straten; Moore–Piepmeyer–Spiroff–Walker)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kurano (2004), Roberts; Hochster (1981); Buchweitz–van Straten; Polishchuk–Vaintrob; Moore–Piepmeyer–Spiroff–Walker

ideas.what: N=2 check: Cl(A) mod algebraic equivalence is finite; the essential part is the continuous group J^1
ideas.modern_name: Structure of divisor class groups of normal surface singularities

missed.claim: A complete conjectural numerology for local Lefschetz theorems on all Chow groups of punctured spectra of isolated singularities. It separates discrete (N^i) and continuous (J^i) parts, gives bijectivity, injectivity and vanishing ranges (up to p-torsion and finite groups), and isolates the critical degrees. Higher-codimension versions of the SGA2 Grothendieck–Lefschetz/Samuel results are still largely open.
missed.quote: Conjectures "Lefschetz" locales ... N^i(X) → N^i(Y) bij exc. p si i ≤ (N-3)/2, inj si i ≤ (N-2)/2 ... Cas critiques J^{(N-1)/2}, J^{N/2}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This gives precise predictions for Chow groups of isolated (e.g. complete-intersection) singularities, an area of current work (Kurano's numerical Chow groups, Srinivas' questions, Kollár's local Lefschetz for Cl). It is a target statement the commutative-algebra community has not formulated in this form.

missed.claim: The vanishing ranges in (1) match exactly the weight constraints on the cohomology of the link of an isolated singularity. Algebraic classes in H^{2i} need weight 2i, impossible when 2i ≥ N; intermediate Jacobian parts likewise. This anticipates by about a decade the semi-purity/weight results of Steenbrink, Durfee and Gabber.
missed.quote: i ≥ N/2  N^i(X) ≡ 0 (mod. groupe fini); i ≥ (N+1)/2 ... J^i(X) = 0
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a motivic or Chow-theoretic reading of link semi-purity, which could be checked via cycle-class maps to local cohomology.

missed.claim: Problem (4) on the next page asks for intersection pairings on N^i of the punctured spectrum and a theory of vanishing cycles in the critical degrees. This prefigures Hochster's theta pairing for isolated hypersurface singularities and its interpretation as a linking or vanishing-cycle form (Buchweitz–van Straten), plus Kurano's numerical equivalence for local rings.

missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It connects the critical Lefschetz degrees for Chow groups with theta/linking pairings. That suggests a systematic framework, not yet in the literature in this generality.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a coherent, previously unrecorded program: higher-codimension local Lefschetz conjectures for Chow groups of punctured spectra, with sharp ranges. Its numerology anticipates later weight and semi-purity phenomena and the theta/linking pairings. It is a natural extension of SGA2, though, and is only conjectural.
transcription_corrections: 'X = S-lt fini' is very likely 'X = S − pt fermé' (the punctured spectrum), which fits 'X, Y réguliers' (isolated singularities) and the N=2 Mumford example.
'A anneau str. local excellent' = 'anneau strictement local excellent'.
In (1), 'i.e. A^i(X) ≡ 0 (mod groupe fini)' applies to the range i ≥ (N+1)/2.
